propagation_experiment.decision: Retain sparse bond-neighbor scans with a temporary stamped domain-membership array; reject packed support tables and binary-search variants because of small-query overhead.
propagation_experiment.scope: Native FragmentQuery.reduce support lookup only. Scientific constraints, witness and completion ordering, branch caps, persistent cache and Python oracle unchanged.
propagation_experiment.method: Mac M4 Pro, one process/thread. Fourteen probes per fresh-process round; 11 timed batches per probe. Prepared calls exclude graph preparation; public calls include it. Real scopes use existing memory_probe.py with identical input, seed/cut order and saved configuration; RSS sampled every 20 ms. No concurrent performance tests.

full_suite.command: PYTHONPATH=src:tests MAPPA_NATIVE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 python -m pytest -q

propagation_experiment.new_critical_cases: 10 cases: sparse occupied/locked destinations, inclusive/exclusive per-edge tolerance boundaries, and a 13-atom path positive / 14-atom path negative into three C6 rings attached through one hub. The hub obstruction independently proves absence.
propagation_experiment.exact_graph_comparison: 265/265 finalized search graphs identical in every dataclass field, including contexts, roots, states, transitions and stops. No mapping-family expansion.
propagation_experiment.limits: The small competing-positive query is 14.85 to 16.10 microseconds in the final paired round. Ring completion stays about 16/32 microseconds. This is not a claim that every call improves or that hard absence queries have a uniform runtime bound. Local tests do not establish cluster throughput. Previous 400-query permutation validation remains historical and was not rerun for this predicate-preserving change.
